role: The abstract button base: a wall-mounted block the player presses to pulse power for 20 (stone) or 30 (wooden) ticks, with arrows keeping wooden buttons down.
scope_reason: The press, release, scheduling and the neighbour pulse exist natively; only the power a receiver would receive is dead (world.conf redstone = off), which is outside this file's behavior.

members.name: BlockButton
members.note: The wooden flag is the only difference between entries 77 (BlockButtonStone) and 143 (BlockButtonWood).

members.name: field_150047_a
members.note: The 143 branch reads it as the tick-length choice (servertick.c:612).

members.name: func_150045_e
members.note: the fallthrough of BlockButton.onBlockPlaced, which ItemBlock.onItemUse calls only after World.canPlaceEntityOnSide passed BlockButton.canPlaceBlockOnSide, the same four side tests on the same unchanged world; no other item places a button

members.name: func_150046_n
members.note: The wooden button's arrow test: func_150043_b's bounds for the metadata as it is (0.125 deep up, 0.0625 down), sr_arrows_in over the projectile pool (pool 2), press or release with the neighbour pulse, the 30-tick reschedule while an arrow is inside (button-arrow-s1).

members.name: onEntityCollidedWithBlock
members.note: Reached from an arrow's func_145775_I (projectile.c arrow_block_collisions, ie_world.on_arrow_button): func_150046_n while up. Any other entity in the cell runs the same arrow test in Java; natively only the arrow's own walk reaches it (an arrow keeps its button down, so an up button with an arrow inside is transient).

members.name: func_150042_a
members.note: The six-neighbour plus attach-block pulse, blockcb.c:1219.

members.name: setBlockBoundsForItemRender
members.note: Same bounds family; render-only: every caller is the client renderer (RenderBlocks, RenderItem, ItemRenderer, RenderGlobal's outline, the item icon and colour hooks); row recordings draw no frames

members.name: getCollisionBoundingBoxFromPool
members.note: Null collision; collide.c:407 lists the buttons.

members.name: canPlaceBlockOnSide
members.note: Needs a normal cube on one horizontal side; place.c's class checks.

members.name: updateTick
members.note: The stone release, and servertick_wood_button for the wooden one (servertick.c update_tick case 77/143).

members.name: onBlockActivated
members.note: The press: set_meta plus blockcb_button_notify plus the schedule, activate.c:624-638.

members.name: isProvidingWeakPower
members.note: world.conf redstone = off: World.isBlockProvidingPowerTo and getIndirectPowerLevelTo return 0 before asking any block (its other callers are the redstone wire, torch and diode power reads, which run only under those)

members.name: isProvidingStrongPower
members.note: world.conf redstone = off: World.isBlockProvidingPowerTo and getIndirectPowerLevelTo return 0 before asking any block

members.name: canProvidePower
members.note: the registry's provides_power flag, which the door, trapdoor, fence gate and rail neighbour branches read (cov-blkpower-s1: a placed button closes an open door, trapdoor and gate)

members.name: onBlockClicked
members.note: Block's empty body overridden empty; a left click on a button (cov-blkbreak-s1) changes nothing

missing: BlockButton.isProvidingWeakPower and isProvidingStrongPower (the power the pressed button emits) are not ported: world.conf redstone = off means nothing receives it.
notes: te-ticks-s1 covers pressing both buttons (DEVLOG 2026-09-25 names the stone and wooden buttons). The press is in the activate machine, the release and the wooden arrow hold are in the scheduled-tick pass (servertick.c), the pulse walk is in blockcb.c. Subclass records: BlockButtonStone and BlockButtonWood carry only the constructor flag and the getIcon texture.
